newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay stocks close lower in range-bound trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stocks close lower in range-bound trade.

text.p: Share prices finished a shade lower at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday as a lack of market-moving news curbed price movements, traders said.
Mirroring the lethargic market mood, the 30-share index of the BSE ended 14.29 points, or 0.46 percent, lower at 3,104.66.
"There is hardly any change in the market trend," said Ashish Ranwala, dealer at Prime Broking, a local brokerage firm.
He said the market was looking to take a cue from first half 1996/97 results of Reliance, due on Friday and the central bank's monetary policy that will be released the next day.
Analysts said Reliance Industries is expected to announce sharply lower profits for the first half due to higher costs, lower product prices and flat volume growth.
"The profits are going to be sharply down," said Jal Irani, petrochemicals analyst at Jardine Fleming India Broking.
Reliance closed 0.25 rupees lower at 188.75 on the BSE.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index lost 5.0 points to 892.77.
Traders said the market was pinning hopes on the Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy for the second half of 1996/97 (April-March) due on Saturday.
The central bank is expected to ease liquidity conditions and put pressure on high interest rates, analysts said.
HDFC and SKF Bearings advanced after both firms posted a rise in their six-month 1996/97 (April-March) net profits on Tuesday.
SKF Bearings gained 150 rupees or 6.12 percent to 2,600 rupees. HDFC rose 52.50 rupees or 2.41 percent to 2,227.75.
The 500-share CRISIL index fell 2.25 points to 599.52 provisional close. SBI lost 2.50 rupees to 208.50, TISCO 1.25 to 170.50, TELCO 2.50 to 418.50 and ITC 0.25 to 310.0.
